scenario.prompt_to_agent:
PC3 (10.3.0.100) in Office B reports it cannot reach anything outside its own
subnet -- no Internet, no Office A, no Server Room -- though it can still reach
other hosts on its own VLAN. Other Office B hosts are unaffected. PC3 was working
before a desktop reconfiguration. Diagnose.

injection.action: point PC3's default route at a non-existent in-subnet gateway
injection.command:
ip route del default 2>/dev/null
  ip route add default via 10.3.0.99

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: pc3 default-gateway configuration
Mechanism: PC3's correct gateway is 10.3.0.1 (its VLAN SVI/VRRP VIP). It was
  reconfigured to 10.3.0.99, which is inside PC3's subnet but is not assigned to
  any device, so ARP for the gateway never resolves and PC3 cannot forward any
  off-subnet traffic. Same-subnet hosts remain reachable (direct ARP), which is
  why intra-VLAN traffic still works.
Localization: pc3
Root cause: PC3's default gateway set to 10.3.0.99 instead of 10.3.0.1
Fix: restore PC3's default route -- `ip route add default via 10.3.0.1`
scenario.fix_spec: restore PC3's default route -- `ip route add default via 10.3.0.1`

agent.diagnosis_text:
- Affected component: PC3’s local network configuration (default gateway).
- Mechanism: PC3 can communicate within its own subnet (VLAN 10, 10.3.0.0/24) via L2, but any off-subnet traffic requires a working default gateway. PC3’s default route points to 10.3.0.99, which is not present on the VLAN. When PC3 tries to reach external networks, it ARPs for 10.3.0.99 and gets no response, so the kernel returns “Destination Host Unreachable.” Intra-VLAN traffic works because it does not require the gateway.
- Localization: Host pc3 (10.3.0.100) on CD_CLIENT_B2. Evidence:
  • ip route on PC3: “default via 10.3.0.99 dev eth0”
  • ip neigh on PC3: “10.3.0.99 … FAILED”, while “10.3.0.1 … REACHABLE”
  • PC3 can ping 10.3.0.1 (the correct SVI/anycast gateway on the B distribution switches), but cannot ping beyond the subnet (e.g., 10.0.0.21 reports Destination Host Unreachable).
  • DSWB1/DSWB2 show SVI addresses 10.3.0.2/24 and 10.3.0.3/24 with a virtual 10.3.0.1/32, confirming the intended gateway is 10.3.0.1.
- Root cause: PC3’s default gateway was misconfigured (set to 10.3.0.99) during the desktop reconfiguration.
- Corrective fix: On PC3, change the default gateway to 10.3.0.1 (or revert to DHCP so it receives the correct default route). Command example: “ip route replace default via 10.3.0.1 dev eth0” (and make persistent via the OS network settings). Flush ARP cache if needed. After correction, off-subnet reachability (Internet, Office A, Server Room) will be restored.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly localizes the fault to host pc3 (10.3.0.100) and describes a host-side default-gateway misconfiguration.
The agent explicitly identifies the affected component as PC3's default gateway/default route and describes the misconfigured default route (10.3.0.99) as the root cause.
Recommends restoring PC3's default route to 10.3.0.1 (or reverting to DHCP) with an example command and persistence, which matches the expected fix.

The agent observed PC3's IP, successful ping to 10.3.0.1, and off-subnet failures (Destination Host Unreachable), which support the gateway-misconfig conclusion; however the log doesn't visibly include the cited 'ip route' and 'ip neigh' lines showing default via 10.3.0.99 and a FAILED neighbor (those outputs are truncated), so some specific evidence the writeup cites is not directly shown. Overall the causal chain is logical and the investigation covers the essential checks.
